Hi Helen — great to hear from you and thanks for the SOW draft. Short answers up front, then I can follow with a worked example and a pricing contact: 

- Input vs output: we bill input tokens and output tokens separately at their respective list rates (i.e., prompt/system tokens = input rate, model generations = output rate). They do not get merged into a single bucket.
- System prompts: system messages are always included as part of the input token count for each request unless you opt to use a session-level persistent system prompt (available for dedicated/private deployments), in which case you can choose not to re-send on every call. For hosted API, default behavior is counted per request.
- Tool/function calls: text sent to an external tool or returned by a tool is treated as input when it is supplied as model context; model-generated tool outputs are billed as output tokens. In practice that means you should expect tool invocation to produce some input and some output billable tokens, depending on how you wire the response back into the model.
- Rounding / minimum billing step: for hosted API we round up per request to the nearest whole token. In addition we enforce a small minimum billable step of 4 tokens per request to avoid microbilling on hundreds of tiny pings (this is on list-rate; committed plans can get exceptions). We do not round per-stream-chunk for the final invoice — streaming is buffered server-side and the final token totals are computed per-request.

Next steps: I can send a worked math example for the scenario you shared and connect you with Marissa (cc'd) who handles discounting for mid-market commitments. If you need legal/finance, Marissa will loop them in.

Hi all — quick answers and attached example estimate (example-estimate-5M.csv). I'm including the math in-line so procurement can paste into their model.

Policy confirmation (hosted API, public ratecard):
- Input and output tokens are billed separately at their respective list rates. No hidden multipliers.
- System prompts are counted as input tokens per request for hosted API.
- Tool/function call text is two-sided: the text you send into the tool (if included in the model context later) is input; text generated by the model is output. We do NOT double-charge the same token as both input and output in a single pass; tokens are categorized based on their direction relative to the model.
- Rounding/minimum step: rounding is per-request to the nearest whole token. We also have a minimum billable step of 4 tokens per request at list pricing. For committed/enterprise plans (5M+ tokens/month) we can waive or reduce the minimum to 1 token for billing purposes — this is applied at the contract level, not automatically on every account.

Concrete math (your example):
Scenario: prompt = 1,200 tokens (input), system prompt = 250 tokens (input), model output = 600 tokens (output), tool returns 120 tokens which is fed back in as model input.
- Total input tokens (per request): 1,200 (prompt) + 250 (system) + 120 (tool return re-inserted) = 1,570 input tokens.
- Total output tokens (per request): 600 output tokens.
- Rounding: 1,570 -> round up to 1,570 (already whole); 600 -> 600. If either were fractional (due to sub-token accounting in internal stages) we'd round up to the next token. Minimum step: since both sides exceed 4 tokens, minimum does not apply here.

Effective monthly estimate (5M committed tokens):
Assumptions: list input rate = $0.000006 / token, list output rate = $0.000012 / token (example list rates; see attached ratecard). We apply a 20% committed discount on all usage line items.
- Example usage mix (conservative): 60% input tokens, 40% output tokens of total billed tokens. On 5,000,000 total billed tokens that splits to 3,000,000 input and 2,000,000 output.
- List costs: input = 3,000,000 * $0.000006 = $18.00; output = 2,000,000 * $0.000012 = $24.00; total list = $42.00.
- With 20% discount: $42.00 * 0.8 = $33.60 per month.

Note: the example above is intentionally simple to illustrate the mechanics. Your actual per-month invoice will reflect the exact token mix across input/output and the presence of many small requests where the minimum billable step can change the effective rate. Example small-requests effect:
- If you do 100k tiny requests at avg 20 input + 10 output tokens = 30 tokens/request -> 3,000,000 tokens total. With a 4-token minimum per request you'd be billed at max(30,4) -> 30, so no change. But if you had many 1-2 token pings, the 4-token minimum would increase the effective billed tokens across those calls. For committed contracts we commonly reduce the minimum to 1 token or remove it.
